A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mixture of Contexts for Long Video Generation. All 17 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching across relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original MoC experiments against dense attention, including multi-shot generation, single-shot generation, Wan-2.1-1.3B results and ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative coherence examples in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Mean-pooled top-k routing, context drop-off/drop-in, mandatory links, causal masking and outer-loop routing are retained. The new per-head/per-layer subsection clarifies routing already described as head-independent in v2 Section 3.3; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: New Figure 4 modestly expands qualitative scenarios to animated multi-shot scenes and sketch-to-building semantic continuity beyond the earlier multi-shot illustrations. Quantitative benchmark coverage is unchanged. Appendix C documents the existing LCT-style training corpus without establishing that a new corpus was introduced between versions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains LCT in Table 1, the native 3B MMDiT base model in Table 2, dense-attention Wan-2.1-1.3B in Table 5, and Flash Attention 2 in the implementation benchmark. Newly cited methods are not added to reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The eight-shot, 480p, 12-FPS evaluation, short-video settings, VBench metrics, training schedules and ablation controls are retained. Dataset processing and corpus sizes are newly documented rather than reported as revised settings. Figure 4 does not specify a distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds five qualitative case studies examining background geometry, sketch/building correspondence, reverse-angle consistency, fine object details and multiple character identities. Existing causality, zero-shot, chunk-size/top-k and forced-link/context-perturbation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the implementation benchmark curves are unchanged. v3 adds Figure 4's qualitative coherence findings and newly asserts routing-memory overhead below 0.1% in Appendix A, although that assertion has no accompanying measurement details.

T1.justification: New Appendix A derives the chunk count N approximately equal to L/C and pooled-key and routing-logit storage costs O(Nd) and O(LN) = O(L^2/C). This adds limited memory-complexity reasoning. Equations (1)–(6) and the outer-loop routing formulation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: learned sparse context retrieval, minute-scale consistency and near-linear efficiency. The claims concerning approximately 85% sparsity, sevenfold attention-FLOPs reduction and 2.2-fold generation speedup are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the CLIP-based pooling rationale with an explanation based on semantic diffusion features and adds an argument that diverse head/layer selections preserve global communication. It also interprets Figure 4 as evidence of detailed semantic and identity retrieval. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands previously sparse training-data documentation: scene/shot segmentation, PySceneDetect, Gemini-1.5 captioning, character-ID conventions, shot-cut markers, approximately 500K authentic scenes and another 1M segmented scenes. v3 also specifies per-head/per-layer routing and custom autograd wrapping. These are substantial disclosures, without evidence of changed training procedures.

R1.justification: v3 adds TECO, NUWA-XL and MALT to the long-video discussion and replaces the CLIP reference and pooling analogy with DDAE. The broader positioning relative to LCT, sparse attention and context-memory approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: Targeted revisions separate Context Drop-off and Context Drop-in, revise the pooling explanation and add routing and coherence paragraphs. Benchmark discussion moves from Section 4 to Appendix B, and memory/data sections precede the retained appendices. The overall narrative and main section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds a five-row Figure 4 with colored detail annotations. The former benchmark Figure 4 moves to the appendix as Figure 5, and the old appendix Figures 5–6 become Figures 6–7. Existing visual content and table structures are retained, with placement and page-flow changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's limited data description, Appendix C makes corpus construction and captioning substantially easier to assess. Routing clarification and annotated coherence examples also improve explanation. The comparative evidence remains unchanged, and the new sub-0.1% memory-overhead assertion lacks supporting measurements, limiting the overall gain.
